[SEG0001] person_1 (DOCTOR): Morning, come through. You can keep him on your lap. What's been going on?
[SEG0002] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): It's his right ear, doctor. He's been screaming at night, and it came on after a cold. I don't know, the days are blurring.
[SEG0003] person_3 (PATIENT): My ear is sore.
[SEG0004] person_1 (DOCTOR): Shame, Leo. Which ear is it?
[SEG0005] person_3 (PATIENT): This one. The right.
[SEG0006] person_1 (DOCTOR): Right ear. Is the crying mostly at night?
[SEG0007] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Ja, nights are the worst. He'll fall asleep and then wake up crying. Daytime he still plays, he's just grumpy.
[SEG0008] person_4 (CAREGIVER): Sorry to jump in. I'm his gogo, I live in with them. It was three nights, not two. I was up walking with him.
[SEG0009] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Three? I thought it was two. Um, well, actually I was on a late shift so I wasn't there the first night, maybe three, I don't know.
[SEG0010] person_1 (DOCTOR): So about two to three nights, we won't force an exact start. Is the cold still hanging on?
[SEG0011] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): The runny nose was last week and that's mostly gone. There's still a bit of a dry cough, not all the time.
[SEG0012] person_1 (DOCTOR): Has he felt hot at all? Any fever?
[SEG0013] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): No. No fever. I've felt him, he's not hot.
[SEG0014] person_4 (CAREGIVER): He was hot, doctor. Last night his forehead was burning. I said so.
[SEG0015] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): I don't think that was a fever. He was under the fleece blanket, crying, so of course he felt warm.
[SEG0016] person_3 (PATIENT): I don't know, doctor.
[SEG0017] person_1 (DOCTOR): That's okay. Did either of you get a thermometer on him, an actual number?
[SEG0018] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): No. Ours packed up and I haven't bought another. So there's no number.
[SEG0019] person_1 (DOCTOR): Any pus or fluid leaking from the ear? Does he pull at it?
[SEG0020] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): No discharge, nothing. He pulls the right ear and then he starts crying.
[SEG0021] person_1 (DOCTOR): Vomiting, runny tummy, or a rash on him at the moment?
[SEG0022] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): No vomiting, no diarrhoea, no rash now. Appetite is down, he left half his porridge. He's drinking, water and some juice.
[SEG0023] person_4 (CAREGIVER): That apple juice he likes. We nearly didn't make it, the robot by the garage was out and the queue was shocking.
[SEG0024] person_1 (DOCTOR): Ag, that corner is always a mess. What have you given him for the pain?
[SEG0025] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Panado, the strawberry syrup, last night and this morning. Maybe five mils, I'm not a hundred percent sure, it might have been a bit less. No ear drops.
[SEG0026] person_1 (DOCTOR): Was that only twice, or on a schedule through the day?
[SEG0027] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Just when he cried. Twice, I think. Not timed properly.
[SEG0028] person_4 (CAREGIVER): I gave him a spoon of the purple cough mixture as well, the bottle from the pharmacy. I don't know the name. It was for the cough.
[SEG0029] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): And before you ask, my sister takes biotin gummies every morning for her hair and she keeps offering them. I didn't give him any, that's hers.
[SEG0030] person_4 (CAREGIVER): I should say, I take a water tablet, the little white one, for my blood pressure. I didn't give him that either.
[SEG0031] person_1 (DOCTOR): Glad you checked. Has he ever had antibiotics, or a reaction to a medicine?
[SEG0032] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Um, long ago he had amoxicillin, the pink one I think, and he got a rash, maybe. I'm not sure it was even from that. I can't remember when, it was ages ago, sometime before he was two. I don't know, doctor.
[SEG0033] person_1 (DOCTOR): A possible rash with the amoxicillin, but you're not sure, and there's no date. Anything else, foods?
[SEG0034] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Not that I know of. No food allergies. Gogo, did you see that rash?
[SEG0035] person_4 (CAREGIVER): I wasn't with them then, so I can't say yes or no. His dad has sugar, diabetes, he takes metformin. That's the father, not Leo.
[SEG0036] person_1 (DOCTOR): Has Leo had ear trouble before? Operations, grommets?
[SEG0037] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): One sore ear last winter, it settled on its own. No operations, no grommets. Otherwise he's well. He does crèche three mornings a week.
[SEG0038] person_1 (DOCTOR): Who's at home day to day?
[SEG0039] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Me and gogo. His dad is away on the mines most weeks. Nobody smokes in the house.
[SEG0040] person_1 (DOCTOR): Leo, I need to look in the ears with a small light. I'll go slowly.
[SEG0041] person_3 (PATIENT): I don't know, doctor. It's sore.
[SEG0042] person_1 (DOCTOR): The right eardrum is red and a little bulging. The left one looks clear, no redness. His throat is mildly red, the chest is clear, and the neck is soft with no stiffness.
[SEG0043] person_1 (DOCTOR): Temperature is 36.9. Heart rate 118, which fits a cross little boy. He's not feverish while he's sitting here.
[SEG0044] person_1 (DOCTOR): I think this is an early middle ear infection after the cold. He's not particularly unwell and we haven't actually measured a fever, so I'd rather watch and wait than start an antibiotic today.
[SEG0045] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Nothing at all? He screamed half the night. I felt a bit hopeless, hey.
[SEG0046] person_1 (DOCTOR): Carry on with the Panado. For his size, strawberry syrup, 7.5 mils of the 120 milligram in 5 mils, up to four times a day, properly spaced, not only once the screaming has started. Leave that purple cough mixture alone, we don't know what it is. And nobody else's pills.
[SEG0047] person_1 (DOCTOR): If he's not better in two days, bring him back. Same if a real fever shows up or the pain gets much worse, don't wait the two days, and then we'll start an antibiotic that isn't amoxicillin, because of that possible rash. No script to fetch today. If he's playing and drinking, crèche is alright; if he's miserable, keep him home.

[SEG0001] person_1 (PATIENT): Hi, sorry I'm late. The parking garage was full, so I circled twice.
[SEG0002] person_2 (DOCTOR): That garage is a nightmare, and this rain didn't help.
[SEG0003] person_1 (PATIENT): I love the rain, it's the humidity that gets me. Anyway, such a week.
[SEG0004] person_3 (CLINICAL_STAFF): Hi again, Maria. I'll get your vitals before the doctor starts.
[SEG0005] person_1 (PATIENT): Sure. My daughter's recital is tonight, so I'm kind of distracted.
[SEG0006] person_3 (CLINICAL_STAFF): Arm out for me. Doctor, numbers are on the screen.
[SEG0007] person_2 (DOCTOR): Thanks, Jess. Maria, how's the lichen planus been?
[SEG0008] person_1 (PATIENT): Up and down. The rash on my wrists came back about four months ago.
[SEG0009] person_2 (DOCTOR): Is it itchy, painful, or both?
[SEG0010] person_1 (PATIENT): Itchy, mostly. I scratch at night and wake up.
[SEG0011] person_2 (DOCTOR): So the itching at night is waking you?
[SEG0012] person_1 (PATIENT): Yes, most nights. Oh, and my mouth too. These sore patches inside my cheeks.
[SEG0013] person_2 (DOCTOR): Tell me about the mouth. When did that start?
[SEG0014] person_1 (PATIENT): Maybe two months back? They sting when I eat spicy food.
[SEG0015] person_2 (DOCTOR): Okay. Any trouble swallowing, or feeling like food is catching?
[SEG0016] person_1 (PATIENT): No, swallowing's fine. Everything goes down okay.
[SEG0017] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any fever or feeling feverish recently?
[SEG0018] person_1 (PATIENT): No fever. Just a scratchy throat last week, probably my son's cold.
[SEG0019] person_2 (DOCTOR): Noted. Any hair falling out, or changes in your nails?
[SEG0020] person_1 (PATIENT): No, hair's the same. Nails are fine too.
[SEG0021] person_2 (DOCTOR): What about joint pain or stiffness?
[SEG0022] person_1 (PATIENT): Nope, my joints are good.
[SEG0023] person_2 (DOCTOR): Let's go over your medications. What are you taking right now?
[SEG0024] person_1 (PATIENT): Okay, so there's the levothyroxine, 50 micrograms in the morning. And the omeprazole, 20 mg before breakfast.
[SEG0025] person_2 (DOCTOR): Good. And for the itching?
[SEG0026] person_1 (PATIENT): The hydroxyzine, 25 mg at bedtime, for the itch. It makes me groggy, but it helps.
[SEG0027] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any creams at the moment?
[SEG0028] person_1 (PATIENT): I ran out of the steroid cream last month. Is that bad?
[SEG0029] person_2 (DOCTOR): No, we'll talk about it. Let me ask about allergies first. Any allergies to medicines?
[SEG0030] person_1 (PATIENT): Yes, sulfa drugs. I got hives from a sulfa antibiotic years ago.
[SEG0031] person_2 (DOCTOR): I'll flag that. Any other medical history besides the lichen planus?
[SEG0032] person_1 (PATIENT): The thyroid, obviously, my underactive thyroid for about ten years. And acid reflux. And I get migraines now and then.
[SEG0033] person_2 (DOCTOR): Okay. How long have you had the lichen planus?
[SEG0034] person_1 (PATIENT): Two years. I was diagnosed after the mouth thing first showed up.
[SEG0035] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any surgeries?
[SEG0036] person_1 (PATIENT): Just my tonsils out as a kid. I was eight, I think.
[SEG0037] person_2 (DOCTOR): Family history? Anything like autoimmune disease, skin problems, diabetes?
[SEG0038] person_1 (PATIENT): My mom has diabetes, type 2. And my dad had melanoma.
[SEG0039] person_2 (DOCTOR): Thanks. Let me ask about habits. Do you smoke?
[SEG0040] person_1 (PATIENT): I quit smoking about ten years ago. I was never a heavy smoker anyway.
[SEG0041] person_2 (DOCTOR): And alcohol?
[SEG0042] person_1 (PATIENT): I drink maybe two glasses of wine a week.
[SEG0043] person_2 (DOCTOR): What do you do for work?
[SEG0044] person_1 (PATIENT): I teach fifth grade. And I live with my husband and the two kids.
[SEG0045] person_2 (DOCTOR): Busy household. Now, any chest symptoms, cough or trouble with your breathing?
[SEG0046] person_1 (PATIENT): No, my breathing's totally fine.
[SEG0047] person_2 (DOCTOR): Good. Let me examine you. Wrists first, then mouth, scalp and nails.
[SEG0048] person_2 (DOCTOR): On both wrists there are flat-topped, purple bumps with fine white lines. Inside both cheeks I see a white lacy pattern.
[SEG0049] person_1 (PATIENT): Is that bad? It looks worse than I thought.
[SEG0050] person_2 (DOCTOR): It's consistent with what we expect. Your scalp has no scarring or bald patches, and your nails look normal.
[SEG0051] person_2 (DOCTOR): Let me read your numbers. Blood pressure is 126 over 80, and pulse is 74.
[SEG0052] person_2 (DOCTOR): Temperature is 36.8 degrees, and oxygen saturation is 99 percent. Weight is 71 kilograms.
[SEG0053] person_1 (PATIENT): Is that okay?
[SEG0054] person_2 (DOCTOR): All reasonable. This looks like an active flare of lichen planus.
[SEG0055] person_1 (PATIENT): So it's not something new? Not something worse?
[SEG0056] person_2 (DOCTOR): It doesn't look like it. But a closer look is sensible.
[SEG0057] person_1 (PATIENT): Meaning what? You're going to cut me?
[SEG0058] person_2 (DOCTOR): A small punch biopsy of the wrist, yes. I'd like to arrange it for next week, under local anesthetic.
[SEG0059] person_1 (PATIENT): Ugh. Okay. Will it scar?
[SEG0060] person_2 (DOCTOR): A tiny mark, no bigger than a pencil eraser.
[SEG0061] person_2 (DOCTOR): I'd also like to order a hepatitis C blood test. It's linked with lichen planus, and we've never checked.
[SEG0062] person_1 (PATIENT): Okay. That makes me nervous.
[SEG0063] person_2 (DOCTOR): Most people test negative. And we'll do a thyroid level too.
[SEG0064] person_1 (PATIENT): Fine. Does the steroid cream matter in the meantime?
[SEG0065] person_2 (DOCTOR): Keep using it in thin layers on the wrists. My staff will renew it.
[SEG0066] person_3 (CLINICAL_STAFF): I can send the refill to your pharmacy today, and the lab slips are ready at the front desk.
[SEG0067] person_1 (PATIENT): Great. And if the rash isn't getting better?
[SEG0068] person_2 (DOCTOR): If it's not improving in six weeks, come back and see me and we'll talk about stronger options.
[SEG0069] person_1 (PATIENT): Okay. Thanks, I'm off to that recital now.
[SEG0070] person_2 (DOCTOR): Good luck, Maria. Drive safely and enjoy the show.

[SEG0060] person_2 (PATIENT): Haan, well. Don't tell my cousin I discussed toilets and pheras in the same breath. See you in four weeks, doctor.

[SEG0044] person_1 (DOCTOR): Your vibration sense is reduced at the ankles.

[SEG0057] person_1 (DOCTOR): Come back in two weeks.
[SEG0058] person_4 (PATIENT): Yes, you know, that's manageable.
[SEG0059] person_1 (DOCTOR): That's all from me. Any questions?

[SEG0001] person_1 (PATIENT): Right. I'm here because my partner says I've got a temper, and I need to sort it. I don't want to lose my job.
[SEG0002] person_2 (DOCTOR): Thank you for coming. Tell me what's been happening.
[SEG0003] person_1 (PATIENT): I get short with people. At work, at home. Small things, someone leaves a door open, and I blow. I shout. Then I feel terrible.
[SEG0004] person_2 (DOCTOR): How long has this been going on?
[SEG0005] person_1 (PATIENT): A year? Maybe longer. I can't say when it started. It got worse after Christmas.
[SEG0006] person_2 (DOCTOR): Has anything changed in your life? ~
[SEG0007] person_1 (PATIENT): A new boss. A new baby, eight months ago. I'm not sleeping, and money's tight. ~
[SEG0008] person_2 (DOCTOR): How's your sleep?
[SEG0009] person_1 (PATIENT): Four hours a night, broken.
[SEG0010] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any thoughts of harming yourself, or anyone else?
[SEG0011] person_1 (PATIENT): No. No, I'd never. Not anyone.
[SEG0012] person_2 (DOCTOR): What are you taking?
[SEG0013] person_1 (PATIENT): Propranolol, 10 mg, when I feel wound up, but not sure it does anything. Something for my stomach, omeprazole, 20 mg. And I take St John's wort, maybe 300 mg, a day.
[SEG0014] person_2 (DOCTOR): I need to stop you there, because St John's wort interacts with a lot of drugs. So it's 300 mg, as you recall it. Any other conditions?
[SEG0015] person_1 (PATIENT): Acid reflux. That's all.
[SEG0016] person_2 (DOCTOR): Do you drink, or use any substances?
[SEG0017] person_1 (PATIENT): A few beers at night, to switch off. Four, five. And lots of coffee.
[SEG0018] person_2 (DOCTOR): And what do you do for exercise, or to relax?
[SEG0019] person_1 (PATIENT): Nothing. No time.
[SEG0020] person_2 (DOCTOR): Let me check your pulse and blood pressure. ~
[SEG0021] person_1 (PATIENT): Fine. ~
[SEG0022] person_2 (DOCTOR): Pulse 84, blood pressure 138 over 88.
[SEG0023] person_1 (PATIENT): Is that okay? ~
[SEG0024] person_2 (DOCTOR): Slightly raised, which fits with stress and the alcohol. Any breathlessness, chest pain?
[SEG0025] person_1 (PATIENT): No.
[SEG0026] person_2 (DOCTOR): Right. Putting this together, irritability and outbursts for a year, poor sleep, a new baby, work stress and heavy-ish drinking, I'd say this is stress-related irritability, probably with sleep deprivation and alcohol feeding it.
[SEG0027] person_1 (PATIENT): Is that all? I thought I might be bipolar or something. ~
[SEG0028] person_2 (DOCTOR): Nothing you've described points that way. But I'd like to check your thyroid and a few other things, because they can cause irritability.
[SEG0029] person_1 (PATIENT): Okay. ~
[SEG0030] person_2 (DOCTOR): Cut the beer to a couple of units, not every night, and stop the St John's wort, it can interact with other things. Cut the coffee after midday.
[SEG0031] person_1 (PATIENT): Right. ~
[SEG0032] person_2 (DOCTOR): And I'd like you to try a short anger-management course, and talking therapy.
[SEG0033] person_1 (PATIENT): Will that help? ~
[SEG0034] person_2 (DOCTOR): It does, for most. I'd like to see you again in three weeks.
[SEG0035] person_1 (PATIENT): Three weeks. Thanks. ~

[SEG0001] person_1 (CLINICAL_STAFF): Mrs Pell's here, doctor, and her husband's come in with her. Blood pressure was one thirty-two over eighty-four, pulse sixty-eight, and seventy-eight kilos on our scales. I can hold a blood-room slot straight after if you end up wanting bloods.
[SEG0002] person_2 (DOCTOR): Thanks. Give me a moment, the screen's frozen solid. Right. Mrs Pell, what's been going on?
[SEG0003] person_3 (PATIENT): Um, I've been tired all the time. I don't know, doctor. Work's flat out, and I'm fifty-three, so I figured it was just the job and getting older.
[SEG0004] person_2 (DOCTOR): How long have you felt this tired?
[SEG0005] person_3 (PATIENT): Months. I can't pin down when it started. I really don't know.
[SEG0006] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): It was March, love. A good five months. She nods off on the couch every arvo, doctor, I've watched her.
[SEG0007] person_3 (PATIENT): Not every arvo. Some days, I'll admit. And I don't know that it was March — could've been later. I don't know, doctor.
[SEG0008] person_2 (DOCTOR): Sorry, say that bit again? The computer just beeped at me. You're not sure it was March?
[SEG0009] person_3 (PATIENT): No. He says March. All I can tell you is months. I don't know any better than that.
[SEG0010] person_2 (DOCTOR): Have you been feeling the cold?
[SEG0011] person_3 (PATIENT): Yeah. Heaps. I'll have a jumper on and the heater going and I'm still cold, hands especially. Been about as long as the tiredness.
[SEG0012] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): She'll sit there with a blanket over her knees. And she's hardly eating, which is the weird part, because she's gone from seventy-one kilos up to that seventy-eight.
[SEG0013] person_3 (PATIENT): The weight, yes. I'm not hardly eating, though. I take the same lunch to work I always have, and if anything there's a bit more toast at night. I don't know where he's got that from.
[SEG0014] person_2 (DOCTOR): OK. So the weight's come up. Was that sudden, or gradual?
[SEG0015] person_3 (PATIENT): Gradual. I don't know, alongside the tiredness, I suppose. Not like, in a week. I did just blame my age.
[SEG0016] person_2 (DOCTOR): And your bowels — any constipation?
[SEG0017] person_3 (PATIENT): No. No, that's all fine. I go regularly.
[SEG0018] person_2 (DOCTOR): How's the mood been?
[SEG0019] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Flat as anything. She won't see anyone on the weekends. Hasn't been herself for months, whatever she tells you.
[SEG0020] person_3 (PATIENT): I'm a bit flat, I'll say that, but it's the work. I'm not avoiding people — we went to my sister's on Sunday. I wouldn't call it depression. I don't know, doctor.
[SEG0021] person_2 (DOCTOR): Sorry, can you do the mood part again? I was clicked into the wrong window.
[SEG0022] person_3 (PATIENT): A bit down when work piles up. I still get everything done. It doesn't feel like a proper illness to me.
[SEG0023] person_2 (DOCTOR): Earlier you said the bowels were fine. Any hard stools, or straining?
[SEG0024] person_3 (PATIENT): Well, actually... yeah. I was wrong before. I've been blocked up the last few weeks. Every second day, or third, and it's hard. I don't know why I told you it was normal.
[SEG0025] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any blood when you go, or pain in the tummy?
[SEG0026] person_3 (PATIENT): No blood. No pain. Just slow, that's all.
[SEG0027] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Doctor, she's been buying those prune packs for ages. I'd call it a couple of months, not a few weeks.
[SEG0028] person_2 (DOCTOR): Alright, I'll note you two don't agree on the timing. Any thyroid problems in the family?
[SEG0029] person_3 (PATIENT): Mum. Underactive thyroid, she was on thyroxine most of her life. Dad's fine, I think. I don't know the ins and outs.
[SEG0030] person_2 (DOCTOR): And have you had your own thyroid checked?
[SEG0031] person_3 (PATIENT): Years ago. They said borderline. I don't know, doctor — maybe six years back, could be longer. I never chased it up.
[SEG0032] person_2 (DOCTOR): Let me get the old path up. Sorry, it's spinning again. Here — TSH back then was 2.1, that's normal, not borderline, and the free T4 was normal too.
[SEG0033] person_3 (PATIENT): Oh. Well, maybe that was the cholesterol they called borderline. I muddle the two. I don't know.
[SEG0034] person_2 (DOCTOR): Happens. Are you taking anything regular, scripts or from the chemist?
[SEG0035] person_3 (PATIENT): Vitamin D, a thousand units, most mornings. I forget it, maybe twice a week. I also had magnesium for a fortnight and then I stopped, about a month ago. My sister swears by it for cramps. I never actually got cramps.
[SEG0036] person_2 (DOCTOR): Vitamin D dose once more? That line didn't stick.
[SEG0037] person_3 (PATIENT): A thousand units. Most mornings. I miss about two a week. I don't know if that's a problem.
[SEG0038] person_2 (DOCTOR): Putting the cold, the tiredness, the weight and the constipation with your mum's history, this could be an underactive thyroid. Could also just be the workload and age. I can't say which yet.
[SEG0039] person_3 (PATIENT): I don't know, doctor. If that's what you reckon. I still think it's work, though.
[SEG0040] person_2 (DOCTOR): Fair enough. We'll get bloods — TSH, free T4, and a full blood count. You don't need to fast.
[SEG0041] person_2 (DOCTOR): Come back in a fortnight either way and we'll look at them together. Keep the vitamin D going as you have been. If the TSH is up we'll talk about thyroxine then — nothing to start today.
[SEG0042] person_1 (CLINICAL_STAFF): I'll walk her round now, doctor. The blood-room slot's still held.

[SEG0003] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Appa, sit properly, you were almost running from the auto.

[SEG0007] person_4 (DOCTOR): Dr. Menon. Is it the knee you came for?
[SEG0008] person_2 (PATIENT): Yes, doctor, the right knee. This BP, whenever I enter a clinic it shoots up, pure white coat. At home I feel absolutely normal, I am telling you.
[SEG0009] person_4 (DOCTOR): Swelling? Giving way? Locking?
[SEG0010] person_2 (PATIENT): No swelling that I have seen, it does not give way, and it does not lock. The ache is worse on stairs, better if I sit with the leg straight for some time.
[SEG0011] person_4 (DOCTOR): Any tablet for it?
[SEG0012] person_2 (PATIENT): I took one Crocin, five hundred milligram, by mouth, the night before last, for the pain, only that single dose, then I stopped. My stomach felt a bit heavy after it, but that settled by morning. I am not on any BP tablet, never have been.
[SEG0013] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Doctor, his father had a stroke, that is why I pushed him to come. I did not want us to ignore a high reading.
[SEG0014] person_4 (DOCTOR): Noted. Diabetes? Heart problem?
[SEG0015] person_2 (PATIENT): No diabetes, no heart problem. BP was never told high before, except these clinic readings, and even those I do not trust.
[SEG0016] person_4 (DOCTOR): Smoke? Alcohol?
[SEG0017] person_2 (PATIENT): I never smoked. Alcohol, only at weddings, maybe twice a year, one small peg, that is all. I am retired from the accounts department at the mill, and I walk to the market most mornings.
[SEG0018] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Appa, do not start on yesterday's match, the doctor has other patients.
[SEG0019] person_2 (PATIENT): No, but it was such a match, doctor, India were fifty for three and I was so tense, then Kohli settled and they crossed two hundred easily. My neighbour was shouting from the balcony the whole evening, very disturbing, but nice also.

[SEG0021] person_2 (PATIENT): Forty minutes, yes, and the driver was playing old Ilaiyaraaja songs, my grandson would have loved it, he is just learning the keyboard, poor boy practices till late.
[SEG0022] person_4 (DOCTOR): Right. Back to the knee. Pain on flat walking?
[SEG0023] person_2 (PATIENT): Flat walking is okay, doctor. Bending is possible, but the last bit on the stairs is where it catches. No fever, no redness, I checked in the mirror this morning, skin looks the same both sides.
[SEG0024] person_4 (DOCTOR): Let me look.
[SEG0025] person_4 (DOCTOR): No swelling, no warmth. Bend and straighten are both full. Tender on the inner side of the right knee. That is all.
[SEG0026] person_1 (NURSE): Second reading, after sitting, one hundred and fifty-six over ninety-two.

[SEG0028] person_4 (DOCTOR): Pulse is eighty-four, regular. I am not calling this established hypertension today.
[SEG0029] person_4 (DOCTOR): It may be white coat. It may be early hypertension. I cannot separate them on two readings.
[SEG0030] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): So no tablet today?
[SEG0031] person_4 (DOCTOR): No tablet today. No point starting a BP medicine on clinic numbers alone.
[SEG0032] person_4 (DOCTOR): Get a home reading morning and evening, sitting, for seven days. Write every number and bring the paper.
[SEG0033] person_2 (PATIENT): We can use my wife's machine, she checks her own pressure, she takes telmisartan forty milligram at night, but that is hers, I have not touched those tablets. I will make a full table, date and time, I am very particular with records from my accounts days.
[SEG0034] person_4 (DOCTOR): One arm only, the right, same each time, after sitting five minutes.
[SEG0035] person_2 (PATIENT): Right arm, five minutes, morning and evening, seven days. And the knee, you are not sending me for any scan?
[SEG0036] person_4 (DOCTOR): No scan now. If it is not better in three weeks, then an X-ray.
[SEG0037] person_4 (DOCTOR): Avoid deep squats, take the stairs slowly. Paracetamol five hundred milligram by mouth, up to three times a day if the pain needs it, with food. Skip it on days you are comfortable.
[SEG0038] person_2 (PATIENT): Three times only if needed, with food, no squats. If the paper shows high BP, which tablet will you give, because my neighbour got a bad cough from one of them and I do not want that kind of trouble.
[SEG0039] person_4 (DOCTOR): We decide after the seven days. I am not naming a tablet now. Come back with the readings in one week.
[SEG0040] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): I will bring him. Should he worry about the stroke thing tonight?
[SEG0041] person_4 (DOCTOR): Not tonight. Pulse is steady and there is no chest pain. If he gets chest pain, a severe headache, or weakness on one side, go to emergency. Otherwise just the one-week visit.
[SEG0042] person_2 (PATIENT): Understood, doctor. One week, readings written properly, knee advice followed, and I will not borrow her telmisartan, promise. Sorry for the long match story, I get carried away.
[SEG0043] person_1 (NURSE): There is no BP medicine to print. Collect the slip for the knee advice at the desk on your way out.
